name: Banalakshmi
why_it_matters: Run by the Vanalakshmi Unmesh Samiti collective at Ramnagar in Sriniketan — about 13-14km from the Visva-Bharati campus. Known for thali-style Bengali meals cooked to order; also sells homemade ghee, pickles and spices made by women's self-help groups in the surrounding villages.
insider_tip: Pre-booking by phone is essential — meals are made-to-order and they don't accept walk-ins for lunch. Book by 10am for the same day; the toto/e-rickshaw from Bolpur takes about 30 minutes.
signature_address: Vanalakshmi Unmesh Samiti, Ramnagar, Sriniketan, Bolpur 731236, West Bengal

name: Sonajhuri Khoai Haat
why_it_matters: The Saturday-only haat (weekly market) inside Sonajhuri / Khoai forest near Shantiniketan — Santhal and local women run open-air stalls of seasonal Bengali street food alongside crafts and baul performances. The food side is essentially a once-a-week pop-up.
insider_tip: Operates Saturday afternoons (3-6pm) only — every other day the forest clearing is empty. Carry small notes; UPI is patchy. Combine with the Khoai Mela morning baul session for the full experience.
signature_address: Khoai Mela ground, Sonajhuri forest, Goalpara, near Shantiniketan, Bolpur 731236

name: Cafe Coffee Day Bolpur
why_it_matters: Bolpur outlet of the national CCD chain — the only proper sit-down café in town with consistent espresso, working AC and Wi-Fi. The de facto study/meeting spot for Visva-Bharati students and visiting parents.
insider_tip: Phone signal is patchier in Shantiniketan than at this CCD; it's the local fallback for video calls. Closes by 10pm; come in the late afternoon to get a power socket.
signature_address: Bhubandanga, near Bolpur Railway Station, Bolpur 731204, West Bengal
